facts: The appellants were owners of 7.35 acres of land being a part of Khasra No. 47/1 in the area of village Manglipeth District Seoni, Madhya Pradesh.

On November 4, 1963, a notification under s. 4 read with Sub-s. (1) of s. 17 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was published in the Government Gazette stating that this land was needed by the State Government for implementation of Seoni Water Supply Scheme.

The appellants filed a claim that they were willing to accept compensation in respect of this land at the rate of Rs.1500/- per acre, 'as the lands adjoining this land and situated in a lesser advantageous position are sold at this rate'.
The Collector made his award on August 17, 1964, whereby he awarded compensation for this land at the rate of Rs.450/per acre.
The appellants made an application under s. 18 of the Act for reference to the District Court for enhancement of the compensation.
Against that judgment, dated May 2, 1967, of the Additional District Judge, an appeal was preferred by the Collector, to the High Court.
issues: Whether the High Court was right in scaling down the compensation to Rs.450/- per acre ?
petitioner_arguments: The appellants had before the acquisition, paid diversion charges to the Government, at the rate of Rs.500/- per acre in respect of the adjoining land, for bringing it into use as building sites.
The land in question is close to a built up quarter of the town, and is within the Municipal limits.

The appellants had intended to parcel out this land into plots and sell the same as building sites and that was why for the adjacent land, he had obtained for that purpose, the permission of the Government by depositing diversion charges at the rate of Rs.500/per acre.
respondent_arguments: There is no evidence to show that the land in question had potential value as building sites.

The existing buildings in the vicinity of this land are old buildings, and the deposit of Rs.500/as diversion charges for the adjacent land made by the appellants, was only a speculative investment with an eye on the distant future.
court_reasoning: There is evidence on the record which unmistakably shows that from the view-point of a willing purchaser, at the relevant time, this land had potential value as building sites.

The circumstance that the appellants had voluntarily paid Rs.500/per acre as diversion charges, for laying out the adjoining land into plots as building sites, was of a clinching character, and taken in conjunction with the other facts, noticed above, conclusively showed that its potential value as building sites was much more than the rate of Rs.450/per acre awarded by the Collector and the High Court.
holding: The total amount awarded for this piece of land after adding solatium at the rate of 15%, was Rs.2,904/-.
He also awarded interest at the rate of 4% from September 19, 1964, on which date the Collector had taken over possession of the land.
